n1.text:
MVP: 25 stores in South Delhi. DCs, stores and devices are dynamic: added in the Master as needed. Settled 23 Nov 2026.

1. DC store in: no QR, no binding.
2. DC store out: a large passport label on each poly bag, box or single item, bound to the Pro box.
3. Travel in the Pro box.
4. Store in: every item gets a small passport label and is bound to the store's HUB fridge, whether it came from the DC or a partner distributor.
5. Store out: at the counter the item is scanned out. For home delivery it is bound to a Pro and the carrier confirms it was delivered. No OTP.
6. The patient scans the item and sees the report. No login.

Identity: every DC and store is known by Apollo's own unique Site ID. Users, devices, work orders and the map all use it.

Carried over from the earlier wireframe so every loop closes: Inventory and GRN, Work Orders, Lite, store to store, and roles for every user.

n2.text:
Settled so far.

The dispatcher types how many items are in each pack, so the store can check the count.

Home delivery needs only the order number. No customer mobile number is taken, because there is no OTP.

The carrier scans the item at the door before tapping Delivered.

An item that could not be delivered goes back into the store fridge.

Site IDs shown (9001 for the DC, 16001 onwards for stores) are samples. The real ones come from Apollo.

Device names: HUB + Site ID, with a letter when a site has more than one fridge or cold room (16007A, 16007B). Pro and Lite: home Site ID + number.

A Pro box means an insulated box with our Pro device in it.

Who carries a work order: own staff or a contract person with a Pro, or a courier with a Lite. A courier never takes a Pro.

One carrier can take packs for many stores in one work order. If one Pro box is not enough, a second Pro is scanned onto the same work order. Each pack is tagged to its store at loading.

Portal login: both ways kept, mobile number with SMS code, and email with password. The phone stays on mobile number and code.

Logistics compliance, not stock keeping: no product name, batch or quantity is held. Item level only at the last leg.

Store to store: the carrier marks Delivered, then the store marks Received by scanning. Courier: Delivered is captured from the link, with no login.

One box carries one product type only. An alert is closed with a remark; closing it never changes a report.

A work order is four picks, all from the Master: from, who carries, device, place. It can be made in the portal or on the phone. Nothing about the product is asked. A pack takes its range from the cold room it leaves, so a DC with a cold room and a deep freezer scans the right room before loading.

Temperature range is by product type (Cold 2 to 8, Frozen -25 to -15, and so on), set by the Super Admin. No product name is kept.

Labels: a site places an order with Track0tic, saying which roll and how many.

Partner distributors are kept by the Super Admin; staff pick from the list, or add a name on the spot if it is not there. The device QR is Track0tic's work. Every report downloads as Excel, CSV or PDF.

The Super Admin is Apollo's top user and can close a stuck trip with a remark.

Compulsory in the Master: only name, mobile number and Site ID. All four drug licence forms (20, 21, 20B, 21B) can be filled for a DC and for a store.

Every work order has a gate pass: printed, or shared by link or on WhatsApp to a number. Previous work orders and their gate passes stay in the portal.

Nothing is fixed to one DC or one number of Pro boxes: DCs, stores and devices are added as needed.

n3.text:
What closes each loop.

Device: sent by Track0tic, GRN, fixed to a site, in use, sent back.
DC to store: store scans the box and packs, box scanned back at the DC.
Pack: opened at the store, items counted against it.
Item: handed over at the counter, or delivery confirmed by the carrier.
Home delivery box: scanned back at the store.
Lite: scanned back at the DC, alert from the 2nd day.
Alert: back in range, or closed with a remark.
Anything stuck: closed by the Super Admin with a remark.
